metadata.name: Libertarianism
metadata.description: US Libertarian Party rights-based libertarianism: personal choice, private enterprise, voluntary assistance and nonintervention. The platform is the specific representative formulation, not every libertarian school.
metadata.period: United States; modern rights-based Libertarian Party formulation
metadata.scope: American individual-rights and free-market libertarianism as articulated in the Libertarian Party platform accessed on the research date, separate from left-libertarian theories and from a strict single-author minarchism. No incumbent government is claimed to implement this doctrine completely. Strict revision-2 re-audit: assess only source-supported positions on the exact questions. Unsupported empirical comparisons, modern technology analogies and institutional particulars remain unknown. Absence of doctrine is not a neutral position. This draft must not be used to calculate or publish a complete profile.
metadata.phrase: A society of voluntary exchange and personal choice in which coercion is limited to defending individual rights.

axes.brief: The scoped US Libertarian Party platform protects individual choice, equal rights and nonaggression. Constitutional accountability is considered as a restraint on power, not majority permission to violate rights. Office does not extinguish the requirement for public accountability.
Armed capacity is not a legitimate source of political authority.
